verification_report.summary: Conditional verification passed for both staged sections and the exact target thm:als-general-measure. The proof was checked sequentially against the stated internal premises; no critical errors or gaps were found. The common-envelope criterion uses finite contact partitions, two monotone capacity limits and weighted extended lower semicontinuity without assuming finite rooftop mass. Its sole conditional inference is the stipulated lemma: p,u in E_phi, p<=u and MAext_theta(p)({p<u})=0 imply p=u, without finite mass. Moving-reference continuity establishes capacity convergence first, then obtains finite limiting mass and weak convergence from uniform total masses and raw sublevel tails. The positive-exponent construction correctly handles continuous positive, bounded measurable and integrable densities. The comparisons using the independently reconstructed minimal-reference theorem satisfy finite exponential order with reference zero; they require neither a lower bound for s nor u_j preceq s, and do not apply the bounded same-theta subsolution theorem to an arbitrary omega-carrier. The zero-exponent argument correctly controls normalization, proves L1(mu) convergence of exp(v_j/j), and identifies the equation by fixed-measure continuity. Positive-exponent solutions and the zero-exponent scalar are unique; uniqueness of the zero-exponent potential is not asserted. The attribution and contextual definitions match [ALS26 v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02339v1). Its general prescribed-reference existence theorem is used only as the target and attribution, never as a premise. No bounded mass hypothesis, automatic finiteness of E_phi, unrestricted L1 mass lower semicontinuity, or general strict-domination premise is used. This verdict does not verify the conditional lemma itself: publication still requires the separate relative_extended_domination_01 audit to pass.
